config.title: Data protection

intro.title: Data protection
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple web application that securely handles user data by implementing basic data protection techniques. You will learn the core concept of input validation to prevent malicious data from being processed. The main technologies involved include HTML forms for data entry and JavaScript for validating and sanitizing user inputs. By the end, you'll understand how to protect data integrity and enhance security in your applications.
intro.usecase: Data protection patterns are essential in any application handling sensitive user information. In banking dashboards, these techniques secure account balances and transaction histories from unauthorized access. E-commerce platforms use data protection to safeguard payment details and personal addresses during checkout processes. Healthcare portals implement these measures to ensure patient records and medical histories remain confidential and HIPAA-compliant.

objectives: Implement basic data encryption for sensitive information
Configure access controls to restrict data visibility
Apply input validation to prevent injection attacks
Initialize secure communication channels for data transmission
Manipulate data with integrity checks to prevent tampering
Integrate data masking techniques for privacy protection

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from 'react' to enable state management in your data protection component.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and hooks
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have access to React and the useState hook for managing state.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported React, but don't forget to also import useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the DataProtection component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named DataProtection that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a component that returns JSX. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the DataProtection component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A DataProtection component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: The component is named DataProtection and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly 'DataProtection' and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you've defined a component named DataProtection that returns a div.

steps.title: Initialize state for sensitive data
steps.instruction: Inside the DataProtection component, initialize a state variable called 'userData' using useState. Set its initial value to an object with properties: name (empty string), email (empty string), and ssn (empty string).
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The initial state should be an object like { name: '', email: '', ssn: '' }.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for user profile
const [profile, setProfile] = useState({ username: '', age: 0 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a state variable 'userData' that will store sensitive user information securely.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an initial object containing name, email, and ssn properties, all set to empty strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure userData is initialized as an object with exactly three properties: name, email, and ssn, all set to empty strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the component, use useState to create a state variable called 'userData' with an initial value of { name: '', email: '', ssn: '' }.

steps.title: Initialize state for data protection status
steps.instruction: Inside your DataProtection component, initialize a state variable called 'isProtected' with an initial value of false using useState.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you already imported to create a new state variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing a boolean state variable
const [isLocked, setIsLocked] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a second state variable that tracks whether data protection is enabled.
successCriteria: The component contains a state variable named 'isProtected' initialized to false using useState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct variable name and initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using useState with the correct syntax and variable name.

steps.title: Define the protectData handler
steps.instruction: Inside your DataProtection component, define a function called protectData that will mask sensitive data and update the protection status.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses setUserData to mask the SSN and setDataProtected to update the protection status.
steps.expectedOutcome: A protectData function is defined that will mask the SSN and set isProtected to true when called.
successCriteria: The protectData function is defined, uses setUserData to mask the SSN, and calls setDataProtected(true).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it properly masks the SSN and updates the protection status.
steps.feedbackWrong: The protectData function should mask the SSN and set isProtected to true. Check the function implementation.

steps.title: Add the main container and title
steps.instruction: In your DataProtection component's return statement, add a div container with a className of 'data-protection' and an h1 title 'Data Protection Demo'.
steps.hint: Start by replacing the current return null; with a div element that has the specified className, then place an h1 element inside it with the title text.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: a container with a title div className="app-container">

My Application
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div with the className 'data-protection' containing an h1 title.
successCriteria: The return statement includes a div element with className='data-protection' and an h1 element with the text 'Data Protection Demo'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the div has className='data-protection' and the h1 contains exactly 'Data Protection Demo'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container or title is missing or incorrect. Please add a div with className='data-protection' and an h1 with 'Data Protection Demo' inside it.

steps.title: Display the user data fields
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add three paragraphs to display the user's name, email, and SSN. For the SSN paragraph, use conditional rendering to mask it (show '***-**-****') when isProtected is true, otherwise show the actual SSN value.
steps.hint: You'll need to access userData.name, userData.email, and userData.ssn. For the SSN, use a ternary operator: {isProtected ? '***-**-****' : userData.ssn}
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying data with conditional masking

Name: {userData.name}

Email: {userData.email}

SSN: {isProtected ? '***-**-****' : userData.ssn}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show three data fields with the SSN conditionally masked based on protection status.
successCriteria: Three paragraphs are added showing name, email, and SSN. The SSN paragraph uses conditional rendering with isProtected to mask the value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some paragraphs, but check that all three fields (name, email, SSN) are displayed and the SSN uses conditional masking based on isProtected.
steps.feedbackWrong: The data fields aren't displayed correctly. Make sure to add three paragraphs and use conditional rendering for the SSN based on the isProtected state.

steps.title: Add the protect button and wire onClick
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your DataProtection component, add a button element with the text 'Protect Data' and wire its onClick event to call the protectData handler function.
steps.hint: Use the <button> element with an onClick attribute that references your protectData function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'Protect Data' button appears in the UI that will trigger the protectData function when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element with text 'Protect Data' is added to the return statement, and its onClick attribute is wired to call the protectData handler.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has the exact text 'Protect Data' and its onClick attribute calls the protectData function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is missing or not properly configured. Add a <button> with text 'Protect Data' and onClick={protectData}.

steps.title: Add the unprotect button and wire onClick
steps.instruction: Add a button with the text 'Unprotect Data' and wire its onClick event to the unprotectData handler function.
steps.hint: Place the button after the existing protect button. Use the onClick attribute to call the unprotectData function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with an event handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Unprotect Data' appears in the UI, which when clicked will trigger the unprotectData handler.
successCriteria: Button element with text 'Unprotect Data' and onClick handler set to unprotectData is added to the component return.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the button has the exact text 'Unprotect Data' and the onClick attribute calls unprotectData.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or incorrectly configured. Add a <button> with text 'Unprotect Data' and onClick={unprotectData}.
